information.description:
Most of the files on Kurt Hansen's military past were classified as top secret following the end of the Unification War. Only top Militech execs and certain members of Congress in Washington have clearance to learn just who this former Colonel truly is. He's the man who secured a foothold for the NUSA in Night City as part of Operation "Midnight Storm". The same man who then, after being abandoned by the NUS government at war's end, built from that foothold a new homeland for himself, all financed by smuggling and arms deals on a global scale.

From Corgo's 77 Collection: Mooks by Corgopolis (Barghest).

description.value: They can get anyone anything, as long as the price is right. Using their charm and skills of trade, they make the deals that keep the economy of the Dark Future flowing.

The shape resembles Paleolithic knives made from splintered bones. Perfect for both wood carving and... flaying. Crude, yet devilishly dangerous — the perfect weapon in the hands of a skilled combatant. A souvenir from Siberia.

Special Features: When this weapon deals damage to a target, until the end of the victim’s next Turn, all subsequent attacks from this weapon on that target deal 1d6 additional damage (4d6). Special Features: Can only load Armor-Piercing Ammunition, which for this weapon costs the same as Basic Ammunition. Ammunition purchased for this weapon can only be used by this weapon. Can only fire in Autofire and Suppressive Fire. Using Autofire with this weapon expends 15 rounds instead of 10.

If there are not 15 rounds left in the magazine, Autofire (Machine Gun 4) expends the entire magazine as Autofire (Machine Gun 3). When using Suppressive Fire with this weapon, the user gets a +2 bonus to their Autofire Check.

If this weapon made an Autofire Attack in the previous Round of combat, its Autofire Rating is increased by 1 to a maximum of Autofire (Machine Gun 7), but it expends 5 additional rounds per Autofire Rating increase (20 Rounds at x5, 25 at x5, and 30 at x7). When rolling for Autofire (Machine Gun 6 or 7) damage, it only requires a single d6 damage die to result in a 6 for it to incur a Critical Injury.

Reloading this weapon requires three Reload Actions. Requires BODY 10+ or paired Cyberarms to not reduce the user’s MOVE by 2 while wielded when the weapon is not Mounted.

  • Matches the core item's setup: the +3 shows as a toggle in the initiative roll dialog.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Cyberware > Neuralware).

Cost: 1,000eb (Very Expensive)

The results of Dynalar’s minimalist approach shows, as while this OS is basically just a slight boost to a reflex booster’s code, it’s still been a standard go-to for soldiers and mercenaries for over a decade now.

Sandevistan Operating System. The Sandevistan can now be activated as half of a ROF 2 Action, and its duration is reduced to 9 seconds (3 Rounds). For the next 3 Rounds after activation, along with Sandevistan’s usual +3 bonus to Initiative, the user can take their Move Action (and only the Move Action) as though they are first in the Initiative Queue, regardless of their Initiative Roll. This allows moving before Demons and Vehicles in the Initiative Queue.

If the user is a Solo, then while Sandevistan is active, whenever they make an Aimed Shot, use a weapon’s Alternate Firing Mode, or make a Martial Arts Special Move Resolution, they may also immediately reassign their Combat Awareness Points without an Action.

Enhances: Sandevistan
Option Slots: 0 (Cyberware Enhancement)

Foundry notes:

  • Every Operating System is incompatible with every other Operating System and with the base cyberware it is for: none of them can be installed while another OS, or that OS's own base cyberware, is anywhere in the user's body or in a worn apparatus they're connected to. The sheet doesn't enforce that.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Operating Systems > Sandevistan Operating Systems).
